claims: "Integrity" is the official name of the Orion spacecraft used for the NASA Artemis II mission.
The name "Integrity" represents trust, respect, candor, and humility.
The crew safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The capsule safely carried four astronauts around the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission was the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
The name "Integrity" reflects the integrated effort, trust, and commitment required from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The spacecraft performed a crew-guided manual piloting test.
The spacecraft performed navigation checks before reentry.
Integrity returned through Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph.
Integrity withstood temperatures near 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit before a safe splashdown.
Upon splashdown on April 10, 2026, the crew reported being in good condition.
The crew was picked up by the USS John P. Murtha.
